forcedChoices.reason: Spanish 'conciencia' also means consciousness, a separate term in the same sentence.
'Actual spiritual status' uses 'actual' in its plain sense, not the actual/potential sense.
'enamorarse' reads as romantic love in Spanish; the context is love of fellows.
'comulgar' carries the sense of taking the Eucharist.
Spanish forces a gender for 'her child'; the masculine generic keeps the sense general.
Spoken to a crowd, so plural 'ustedes'; 'he aquí' reads as archaic.
'parent' has no gender in English; 'padre' would close it to father.
Glossary gives fairness = equidad; 'candid' as 'cándido' is a false friend (naive), so 'directo' for candid and 'franco' for frank.
